note.explanation: Temperature affects different solutes in different ways. Many solids dissolve better in warmer water, but some substances change very little or become less soluble. Gases generally become less soluble as water gets warmer.
examples: KNO₃ becomes much more soluble as temperature increases.
NaCl solubility changes very little with temperature.
note.checkAnswer: Most solid solutes become more soluble as temperature rises, but this is not a rule for every substance. Gases generally become less soluble.
note.simple: Heating often lets water dissolve more solid, but not always. It usually makes water hold less gas.
note.checkQuestion: What usually happens to the solubility of a gas in water when the temperature increases?
note.title: Temperature and solubility
steps: Remember the definition: solubility is measured for 100g of solvent at a particular temperature.
Check the substance: different solutes respond differently to temperature.
For many solids, heating increases solubility; for some, it changes little or decreases.
For gases, solubility in water generally decreases as temperature increases.
note.answer: The solubility of a gas in water generally decreases when the temperature increases.

options: It first decreases and then increases
mcqs.stem: What generally happens to the solubility of a gas in water when the temperature increases?
rationales: This is incorrect because the textbook states that gas solubility generally falls as temperature rises.
This is correct because gases are generally less soluble in warmer water.
This is incorrect because gas solubility usually changes with temperature rather than staying exactly constant.
This is incorrect because the stated general trend is a decrease, not a decrease followed by an increase.

mcqs.stem: Which substance is given as an example of one whose solubility increases as temperature increases?
rationales: This is correct because the textbook lists potassium nitrate (KNO₃) among substances whose solubility rises with temperature.
This is incorrect because lithium carbonate is given as a substance whose solubility decreases with temperature.
This is incorrect because calcium chromate is given as a substance whose solubility decreases with temperature.
This is incorrect because the textbook states that calcium hydroxide solubility decreases as temperature increases.

options: It becomes the same as KNO₃
mcqs.stem: How does the solubility of sodium chloride in water respond to an increase in temperature?
rationales: This is incorrect because the textbook says sodium chloride solubility does not increase appreciably.
This is incorrect because no claim is made that its solubility falls to zero.
This is correct because sodium chloride solubility changes very little as temperature rises.
This is incorrect because sodium chloride does not acquire the temperature response of KNO₃.

mcqs.stem: A saturated sugar solution is prepared at room temperature. What does the activity suggest doing to dissolve more sugar?
rationales: This is incorrect because cooling is not the action used in the activity to dissolve more sugar.
This is correct because heating the saturated solution increases the amount of sugar that can dissolve.
This is incorrect because stirring or shaking alone is not the temperature change described as increasing solubility.
This is incorrect because adding water changes the amount of solvent rather than showing the effect of temperature.

mcqs.stem: Which substance is most suitable for purification by crystallization from hot water, using the strong increase in solubility with temperature described in this section?
rationales: This is correct because KNO₃ solubility increases strongly with temperature, so cooling can cause crystals to form.
This is incorrect because NaCl solubility does not increase appreciably with temperature.
This is incorrect because Li₂CO₃ solubility decreases as temperature increases.
This is incorrect because CaCrO₄ solubility decreases as temperature increases.

options: The solubility of KNO₃ falls as temperature rises

rationales: This is incorrect because the plotted KNO₃ curve slopes upward as temperature rises.
This is correct because the graph shows more KNO₃ dissolving per 100 g of water at higher temperatures.
This is incorrect because KNO₃ is shown as a solute in water, not as a gas.

mcqs.stem: Why are soda water bottles stored in a refrigerator?
rationales: This is correct because carbon dioxide is more soluble at low temperature and stays dissolved longer.
This is incorrect because warming makes carbon dioxide less soluble in water.
This is incorrect because an open bottle allows dissolved carbon dioxide to escape.
This is incorrect because heating decreases gas solubility rather than helping retain the carbon dioxide.

rationales: This is incorrect because solubility is not a fixed claim that 100 g of solute must be present.

written.text: How variation of solubility at different temperatures can be useful for us?
written.finalAnswer: Temperature-dependent solubility can be used to purify solids by crystallization; low temperatures also help keep gases such as carbon dioxide dissolved in water.

rubric.why: The answer must connect the usefulness to changes in solubility with temperature.
rubric.description: Relate the usefulness to temperature-dependent solubility.
rubric.how: State that solubility changes when temperature changes.

rubric.why: Purification by crystallization is the main use of changing solid solubility described in the text.
rubric.description: Give purification of solids by crystallization.
rubric.how: Explain that a solid can be purified by dissolving it and forming crystals.

rubric.why: The section also applies temperature-dependent solubility to gases.
rubric.description: Give the low-temperature gas example.
rubric.how: Mention that carbon dioxide is more soluble in cold water.

rubric.why: This links the gas-solubility idea to a familiar practical use.
rubric.description: State the practical use of refrigerating soda water.
rubric.how: Say that soda water is refrigerated to keep carbon dioxide dissolved longer.

modelAnswer: The increase in the solubility of solids in liquids with increase in temperature may be used to purify them.
Pure solids commonly appear as beautifully shaped crystals.
Carbon dioxide gas is more soluble in water at low temperature.
Soda water bottles are stored in the refrigerator to keep carbon dioxide gas dissolved in water for a longer period of time.
Therefore, variation of solubility with temperature is useful for purification by crystallization and for keeping gases dissolved.

written.text: Q1.6. Why do different compounds have different solubilities in water at a particular temperature?
written.finalAnswer: Different compounds have different solubilities because each compound has its own nature and interacts differently with water at a particular temperature.

rubric.why: The response should directly address the difference between compounds.
rubric.description: State that compounds have different characteristic solubilities.
rubric.how: Say that each compound has its own solubility in water.

rubric.how: State that compounds interact with or dissolve in water to different extents.

rubric.description: Keep the comparison at the stated temperature.

modelAnswer: Different compounds have different natures and properties.
They interact with and dissolve in water to different extents.
Therefore, at a particular temperature, each compound has a different solubility in water.

written.text: Q1.7. Why NaCl can not be crystallized from water just like KNO₃?
written.finalAnswer: The solubility of NaCl in water does not increase appreciably with temperature, whereas the solubility of KNO₃ increases greatly; therefore, cooling does not crystallize NaCl from water in the same way.

rubric.why: This is the key fact that explains why NaCl behaves differently.
rubric.description: State how NaCl solubility responds to heating.
rubric.how: Say that its solubility does not increase appreciably with temperature.

rubric.why: The comparison with KNO₃ is essential to answering the question.
rubric.description: State that KNO₃ solubility increases substantially with temperature.
rubric.how: Compare the strong increase for KNO₃ with the small change for NaCl.

rubric.why: Crystallization on cooling depends on a useful change in solubility.
rubric.description: Connect the temperature difference to crystallization on cooling.
rubric.how: Explain that cooling a hot solution does not reduce NaCl solubility enough in the same way.

rubric.why: The final statement must answer why the two substances cannot be crystallized alike.
rubric.description: Give the conclusion about the different crystallization behaviour.
rubric.how: Conclude that NaCl cannot be crystallized from water just like KNO₃.

modelAnswer: The solubility of NaCl in water does not increase appreciably with the increase in temperature.
The solubility of KNO₃ increases with the increase in temperature.
On cooling, the solubility of KNO₃ changes enough for crystals to form.
Therefore, NaCl cannot be crystallized from water just like KNO₃.

written.text: Q1.4. Define solubility of a solute. How does the solubility of solutes change with the increase in temperature?
written.finalAnswer: The solubility of a solute is the amount of solute which can dissolve in 100g of a solvent at a particular temperature. Usually the solubility of solids increases with temperature, but this is not a general rule: some solubilities change little or decrease, and the solubility of gases in water generally decreases.

rubric.why: The full definition, including the reference amount and temperature, is central to the question.

rubric.how: State the amount of solute that dissolves in 100g of solvent at a particular temperature.

rubric.how: Mention that some substances change very little or become less soluble.

rubric.why: The temperature trend for gases is an important contrast with many solids.
rubric.description: State the usual temperature effect on gases dissolved in water.
rubric.how: Say that gas solubility generally decreases as temperature increases.

modelAnswer: The solubility of a solute is the amount of solute which can dissolve in 100g of a solvent at a particular temperature.
Usually the solubility of solids increases with the increase in temperature, but it cannot be taken as a general rule.
The solubility of sodium chloride does not increase appreciably with the increase in temperature.
The solubility of lithium carbonate and calcium chromate decreases with the increase in temperature.
The solubility of gases in water also decreases with the increase in temperature.

written.text: Q1.1. Preparation of solutions leads to an important process in chemistry which enables us to purify a compound through crystallization. Describe a process in which potassium nitrate is purified by crystallizing it in water.
written.finalAnswer: Dissolve impure potassium nitrate in hot water to make a saturated solution, then cool the solution so potassium nitrate crystals form. Separate the crystals from the remaining solution and dry them.

rubric.why: Hot water dissolves more KNO₃ because its solubility increases with temperature.
rubric.description: Prepare the hot solvent containing the impure solid.
rubric.how: Dissolve impure potassium nitrate in hot water.

rubric.why: A saturated hot solution is needed so crystals can form as solubility falls on cooling.
rubric.description: Make the solution saturated while hot.
rubric.how: Add or dissolve the solid until the hot solution is saturated.

rubric.why: Cooling lowers the amount of KNO₃ that stays dissolved and allows crystals to form.
rubric.description: Cool the solution to produce crystals.
rubric.how: Let the hot saturated solution cool.

rubric.why: The crystals must be separated from the remaining solution.
rubric.description: Separate the formed crystals.
rubric.how: Filter or otherwise separate the crystals from the solution.

rubric.why: Drying gives the purified crystalline product.
rubric.description: Finish with dry purified crystals.
rubric.how: Dry the separated crystals.

modelAnswer: Dissolve the impure potassium nitrate in hot water to prepare a saturated solution.
Allow the hot solution to cool.
Potassium nitrate crystals form as the solution cools.
Separate the crystals from the remaining solution by filtration.
Dry the crystals to obtain purified potassium nitrate.

examTips: A short-answer question may ask for the definition of solubility; include both “100g of a solvent” and “at a particular temperature.”
A constructed-response or descriptive question may ask how temperature affects solubility. Give the usual trend, then state that it is not a general rule.
Use examples accurately: KNO₃ solubility increases greatly; NaCl does not increase appreciably; Li₂CO₃, CaCrO₄, calcium hydroxide and gases become less soluble as temperature rises.
A crystallization answer earns marks for explaining the hot saturated solution, cooling, crystal formation and separating/drying the crystals.
For an application question, connect low temperature with carbon dioxide staying dissolved in soda water.

hints: Compare how NaCl and KNO₃ respond when heated.
Cooling forms crystals effectively when a substance's solubility has increased substantially on heating.

steps.why: The activity begins with a solution already saturated at room temperature.
steps.text: Take 100 g of water in a beaker and prepare saturated solution of sugar at room temperature.

steps.why: Heating tests whether the amount of sugar that can dissolve changes with temperature.
steps.text: Heat the beaker on a spirit lamp.

steps.why: Adding more sugar checks whether the warmer solution can dissolve additional solute.
steps.text: Add a little more sugar in it and stir it.

steps.why: The textbook observes that heating increases the quantity of sugar dissolved in water.
steps.text: By heating the solution the quantity of sugar dissolved in water has increased i.e. the solubility of sugar has increased.

example.question: Take 100 g of water in a beaker and prepare saturated solution of sugar at room temperature. Heat the beaker on a spirit lamp. Add a little more sugar in it and stir it. Will this sugar be dissolved in it?
example.answer: Yes. By heating the solution, the quantity of sugar dissolved in water increases; the solubility of sugar has increased.

explain.title: What solubility means
explain.body: The solubility of a solute is the amount of solute which can dissolve in 100g of a solvent at a particular temperature. Always include the amount of solvent and the temperature when you give the definition.

explain.title: Temperature does not affect every substance in the same way
explain.body: Many solids, including potassium nitrate (KNO₃), silver nitrate (AgNO₃) and potassium chloride (KCl), become more soluble as temperature rises. But this is not a general rule. Sodium chloride changes very little, while lithium carbonate (Li₂CO₃), calcium chromate (CaCrO₄) and calcium hydroxide become less soluble.

explain.title: Gases and useful applications
explain.body: The solubility of gases in water generally decreases as temperature increases. Carbon dioxide is more soluble in cold water, so soda water bottles are stored in a refrigerator to keep the gas dissolved longer. The increase in solubility of many solids when heated can also be used to purify them by crystallization.

mistakes: Defining solubility without saying “in 100g of a solvent” or “at a particular temperature.”
Writing that the solubility of every solid increases with temperature; the textbook says this is not a general rule.
Mixing up the examples: NaCl changes little, while Li₂CO₃ and CaCrO₄ become less soluble as temperature rises.
Claiming that gases become more soluble in warm water; gases generally become less soluble.
Describing crystallization without explaining that the hot solution is cooled so crystals form.
